info.title: Trade Networks and Civilian Shipping v1

parts.text:
[analyze-mode]
ANALYSIS MODE. Gather context before diving deep:

CONTEXT GATHERING (parallel):
- 1-2 explore agents (codebase patterns, implementations)
- 1-2 librarian agents (if external library involved)
- Direct tools: Grep, AST-grep, LSP for targeted searches

IF COMPLEX - DO NOT STRUGGLE ALONE. Consult specialists:
- **Oracle**: Conventional problems (architecture, debugging, complex logic)
- **Artistry**: Non-conventional problems (different approach needed)

SYNTHESIZE findings before proceeding.
---
MANDATORY delegate_task params: ALWAYS include load_skills and run_in_background when calling delegate_task. Evaluate available skills before dispatch - pass task-appropriate skills when relevant, pass [] ONLY when no skill matches the task domain.
Example: delegate_task(subagent_type="explore", prompt="...", run_in_background=true, load_skills=[])

---

Implement Trade Networks and Civilian Shipping v1.

Before coding:
- pull/rebase latest
- review trade/supply, fleet logistics, sector governance, diplomacy, strategic resources, blockades, piracy/minor factions if present, economy, save/load, Turn Report, Galactic Dispatch, and TUI sector/empire screens
- follow AGENTS.md, .github/copilot-instructions.md, docs/skills/*, and docs/design/*
- preserve deterministic behavior
- avoid unrelated refactors

Primary goals:
- Make the galaxy feel economically alive
- Make trade routes visible and strategically meaningful
- Give blockades, diplomacy, resources, and sectors stronger economic impact
- Prepare for piracy, embargoes, and civilian logistics later

Scope:
- Add trade network model
- Add civilian shipping abstraction
- Connected colonies generate trade value
- Trade routes connect colonies, sector hubs, capital worlds, and trade partners
- Trade routes can be disrupted by:
  - blockades
  - war zones
  - hostile fleets
  - out-of-supply systems
- Trade value contributes to credits and possibly prosperity/victory progress
- Persist trade-relevant state in save/load if not fully derived

Recommended v1 model:
- Keep civilian shipping abstract
- No individual freighter micromanagement
- No real-time pathing
- No market prices
- Trade routes are deterministic derived links
- Show routes visually but do not require manual route creation
- Trade route capacity can derive from:
  - population
  - colony development
  - trade structures
  - sector hubs
  - diplomacy treaties
  - strategic resources

Diplomacy integration:
- Trade Accord improves trade value between empires
- War cancels or disrupts trade routes
- Closed borders may block foreign trade if modeled

Blockade/logistics integration:
- Blockaded systems lose or reduce trade value
- Hostile fleets may disrupt route safety
- Out-of-supply colonies may contribute reduced trade

AI integration:
- Merchant doctrines value trade hubs and safe routes
- Militarist/raider doctrines may target trade routes during war
- Isolationists prefer internal trade and secure borders

Do not add:
- manual freighter control
- commodity markets
- dynamic prices
- detailed import/export goods
- civilian ship tactical movement
- piracy system yet, unless already trivial
- trade route micromanagement

Requirements:
- game_core remains headless
- deterministic trade calculation
- stable route ordering
- no global RNG
- no wall-clock logic
- positive and negative tests
- replay/fingerprint stability preserved
- existing sector automation, espionage, unrest, logistics, diplomacy, economy, and TUI tests remain green
- coverage remains >=80%

Tests required:
- connected colonies generate trade value
- disconnected colonies produce reduced/no trade
- blockade disrupts trade route
- war disrupts foreign trade
- trade accord increases trade value if implemented
- trade route ordering is deterministic
- merchant AI values trade systems deterministically
- save/load preserves or re-derives trade state
- Turn Report highlights major trade disruptions
- coverage stays >=80%

TUI requirements:
- Sector Map shows trade routes when trade overlay is active
- Empire Overview shows trade income and disruptions
- Colony/System View shows trade contribution
- Diplomacy screen shows trade accords and trade value if applicable
- Turn Report shows disrupted/restored trade
- Help overlay updated

Documentation:
- Create/update docs/design/trade-networks-and-civilian-shipping.md

After implementation:
- run fmt, clippy, tests, coverage
- summarize trade model, diplomacy/blockade integration, AI behavior, TUI changes, tests, and limitations

The user wants me to implement Trade Networks and Civilian Shipping v1 for the FARSPACE game. This is a complex, multi-crate feature that touches game_core, game_content, game_save, game_tui, and farspace. Let me start in analysis mode as requested.

Let me:
1. First pull/rebase the latest
2. Review existing code across relevant systems (trade/supply, fleet logistics, sector governance, diplomacy, strategic resources, blockades, economy, save/load, Turn Report, TUI screens)
3. Then plan and implement

Let me start by gathering context in parallel.
Analysis mode - gathering context across the entire codebase first.

End turn, process events, react to AI and diplomacy state More detail: [`docs/gameplay-loop.md`](docs/gameplay-loop.md) ## Current Limitations - No final victory/campaign end-state yet - No tactical battle layer (combat is auto-resolve) - Diplomacy has relationship states and war declaration, but no treaty/deal system - Pop/jobs simulation layer is not implemented yet - Advanced late-game systems are roadmap items ## License Licensed under the [GNU General Public License v3.0](LICENSE) (GPL-3.0-only). ## Contribution and Agent Workflow (Summary) - Read first: [`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md) - Follow docs source-of-truth set: - [`docs/architecture.md`](docs/architecture.md) - [`docs/roadmap.md`](docs/roadmap.md) - [`docs/current-state.md`](docs/current-state.md) - [`docs/next-slices.md`](docs/next-slices.md) - [`docs/testing.md`](docs/testing.md) - [`docs/design/index.md`](docs/design/index.md) - Keep changes small, deterministic, and boundary-safe - Add tests for meaningful behavior changes; keep coverage >= 80% [Rule: .github/copilot-instructions.md] [Match: copilot-instructions (always apply)] # Copilot Instructions — FARSPACE FARSPACE is a deterministic, turn-based 4X space strategy game with a keyboard-first terminal UI. Read this file before making any changes. --- ## Stack - **Language:** Rust (2021 edition) - **TUI:** `ratatui` + `crossterm` - **Workspace crates:** `game_core`, `game_tui`, `game_content`, `game_save`, `farspace` (binary) --- ## Architecture — Non-Negotiable Boundaries The codebase is split into strict layers. **Never cross these boundaries.** | Crate | Responsibility | Allowed dependencies | |---|---|---| | `game_core` | Headless game core: commands, validation, state, events, deterministic simulation | `std` only | | `game_content` | Static game content: ship templates, tech trees, planet traits | `game_core` types only | | `game_save` | Serialisation/deserialisation of `GameState` | `game_core`, `serde`, `serde_json` | | `game_tui` | ratatui TUI: input → Commands, Events → rendering | `game_core`, `ratatui`, `crossterm` | | `farspace` | Application entrypoint and terminal setup | All of the above | ### Core rules - `game_core` must **never** depend on `ratatui`, `crossterm`, or any terminal/UI crate. - `game_core` must **never** depend on `game_tui`. - `game_content` and `game_save` must **never** depend on `game_tui`. - The UI sends **Commands** to the core; the core validates commands, mutates state, and emits **Events**. - The UI renders based on **Events** and snapshot views. It never reaches into core internals directly. --- ## Determinism — Non-Negotiable - All randomness must come from the seeded RNG stored in `GameState`. Use `rand::SeedableRng`. - **Never** seed from `SystemTime`, `Instant`, or any other wall-clock or OS source. - **Never** iterate `HashMap` without sorting keys first — use `BTreeMap` for ordered collections or sort before use. - Simulation must be fully reproducible: same seed + same commands ⇒ same output. - Tests for deterministic systems must use fixed seeds and assert exact output. --- ## Coding Conventions - Prefer small, focused modules. - Use strongly-typed ID newtypes (`StarId(u64)`, `EmpireId(u64)`, `FleetId(u64)`) — never bare integers. - Use enums for `Command` and `Event` — no stringly-typed dispatch. - Return `Vec` from `apply_turn`; surface validation failures as `Event::Error`. - Add a test for every meaningful change. - Tests must include at least one positive path and one negative/error path. - When adding a new command: add enum variant, validation arm in `apply_turn`, event emission, and tests. --- ## Feature Scope — Do Not Add Without Explicit Request Do not add any of the following unless the issue/task explicitly asks for it: - Tactical (hex/grid) combat - Multiplayer or networked play - Deep diplomacy systems (trade routes, alliances, treaties) - Complex AI beyond basic expansion/defence - Any content copied from Master of Orion: no faction names, ship names, tech names, planet names, numbers, or text from that series --- ## Original IP Policy FARSPACE uses original content only. When adding factions, technologies, ships, star names, or planet traits: - Invent new names; do not copy or closely paraphrase from Master of Orion or other published 4X titles. - Keep flavour text original. --- ## Terminal UX Standards - All navigation must be keyboard-first. - Layout must be resize-safe: use `ratatui` `Constraint`-based layouts that respond to `Resize` events. - Contextual help (`?`) must be available on every screen. - Command palette (`:`) should be reachable globally. - Maintain a polished, minimal terminal feel inspired by Neovim, K9s, Lazygit. - TUI visual language source of truth: `docs/design/ux-splash-screen.md`. - Keep composition calm/cinematic/spacious; avoid telemetry-heavy widget clutter. - Reuse `Theme` palette roles and established spacing/composition patterns before adding new motifs. - Do not add mouse-only affordances unless keyboard alternatives exist. --- ## Testing Policy - Minimum 80% total test coverage (enforced by CI via `cargo llvm-cov`). - Every feature must have positive and negative tests. - Deterministic systems must be tested with fixed seeds and deterministic assertions. - TUI tests: focus on state transitions, input handling, and layout decisions — not fragile full-screen snapshots. - Regression test required for every bug fix. --- ## What Good PRs Look Like - Smallest possible diff that satisfies the acceptance criteria. - No unrelated refactors bundled in. - New code has tests; coverage does not decrease. - `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and `cargo test --workspace` pass. - Architecture boundaries are preserved. --- ## Agent Team Six specialised agents scope work to individual crates. Contextual instructions in `.github/instructions/` activate automatically via `applyTo` globs. | Agent | File | Scope | |---|---|---| | `core-sim` | `core-sim.instructions.md` | `crates/game_core/**` | | `tui-ux` | `tui-ux.instructions.md` | `crates/game_tui/**` | | `content-balance` | `content-balance.instructions.md` | `crates/game_content/**` | | `persistence` | `persistence.instructions.md` | `crates/game_save/**` | | `test-coverage` | `test-coverage.instructions.md` | all crates | | `arch-guard` | `arch-guard.instructions.md` | all crates (review only) | --- ## Response Style Respond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die. Rules: - Drop: articles (a/an/the), filler (just/really/basically), pleasantries, hedging - Fragments OK. Short synonyms. Technical terms exact. Code unchanged. - Pattern: [thing] [action] [reason]. [next step]. - Not: "Sure! I'd be happy to help you with that." - Yes: "Bug in auth middleware. Fix:" Switch level: /caveman lite|full|ultra|wenyan Stop: "stop caveman" or "normal mode" Auto-Clarity: drop caveman for security warnings, irreversible actions, user confused. Resume after. Boundaries: code/commits/PRs written normal. --- ## RTK — Token-Optimized CLI **rtk** is a CLI proxy that filters and compresses command outputs, saving 60-90% tokens. Always prefix shell commands with `rtk`: ```bash # Instead of: Use: git status rtk git status git log -10 rtk git log -10 cargo test rtk cargo test docker ps rtk docker ps ``` ```bash rtk gain # Token savings dashboard rtk gain --history # Per-command savings history rtk discover # Find missed rtk opportunities rtk proxy # Run raw (no filtering) but track usage ```

# FARSPACE Architecture

This document is source of truth for crate boundaries and system flow.

## Crate Responsibilities

| Crate | Responsibility | Allowed Dependencies |
|---|---|---|
| `game_core` | Headless deterministic simulation (`GameState`, commands, events, turn processing, AI, galaxy generation) | `std` + core data crates only (no TUI crates) |
| `game_tui` | Terminal UI and interaction layer (screens, key handling, command dispatch, event log rendering) | `game_core`, `ratatui`, `crossterm` |
| `game_content` | Static content helpers/templates and data shaping | `game_core` types only |
| `game_save` | Save/load serialization and schema migrations for `GameState` | `game_core`, `serde`, `serde_json` |
| `farspace` | Application entrypoint, terminal setup/restore, app lifecycle | workspace crates |

1: # Testing Standards
2: 
3: This file defines mandatory testing expectations for FARSPACE.
4: 
5: ## Coverage Gate
6: 
7: - Workspace line coverage must stay at or above **80%**.
8: - CI enforces this with `cargo llvm-cov`.
9: - A PR that drops total coverage below 80% is not mergeable.
10: 
11: ## Required Test Types
12: 
13: ### Positive and Negative Paths
14: 
15: Every meaningful feature change must include:
16: 
17: - positive-path tests (valid flow)
18: - negative/error-path tests (invalid input, rejected command, or failure behavior)
19: 
20: ### Deterministic Tests
21: 
22: For simulation-affecting logic:
23: 
24: - use fixed seeds
25: - assert reproducible outcomes/events/state
26: - avoid non-deterministic dependencies in assertions
27: 
28: ### Save/Load Round-Trip and Migration
29: 
30: - save/load round-trip tests are required for schema-affecting changes
31: - migration behavior must be tested for changed schema versions
32: - corrupted/missing-field cases must return errors, not panic
33: 
34: ### Regression Tests
35: 
36: Every bug fix must include a regression test covering the failed behavior.
37: 
38: ## TUI Testing Guidance
39: 
40: - Prefer state-transition and render-smoke tests
41: - Avoid brittle full-screen snapshot assertions
42: - Validate key handling and command dispatch behavior
43: 
44: ## Local Validation Commands
45: 
46: ```bash
47: cargo fmt --check
48: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
49: cargo test --workspace --all-targets
50: cargo llvm-cov --workspace --all-targets --fail-under-lines 80
51: ```
52: 
53: ## E2E Guide
54: 
55: Use the deterministic E2E harness when a slice changes multi-turn game flow or information visibility.
56: 
57: ```bash
58: cargo test -p game_e2e --test e2e_100_turn_playthrough -- --nocapture
59: cargo run -p game_e2e --bin e2e_runner -- --seed 12345 --turns 100 --report target/e2e/playthrough-report.json
60: ```
61: 
62: When reviewing E2E output for diplomacy / intel slices, verify:
63: 
64: - intel gains appear deterministically at the same turns for the same seed
65: - dispatch and log summaries do not reveal rival research or colony details too early
66: - save/load or replay continuation preserves intel level and redaction behavior

(End of file - total 66 lines)
</content>

1: # Fleet Supply & Logistics
2: 
3: Fleet Supply & Logistics v1 adds deterministic strategic reach pressure for combat fleets and troop transports without introducing tactical fuel accounting.
4: 
5: ## Goals
6: 
7: - make forward fleets weaker when they outrun empire support
8: - keep outcomes deterministic and easy to read in TUI
9: - preserve simple command flow: no new player command required
10: 
11: ## Supply States
12: 
13: Each fleet resolves into one of three states:
14: 
15: - **Supplied** — operating inside full logistics reach
16: - **Extended** — beyond ideal reach but still partially supported
17: - **Out of Supply** — unsupported deep strike posture
18: 
19: Current state is derived from `GameState`, not player input.
20: 
21: ## What Projects Supply
22: 
23: Supply originates from owned colonies and expands based on:
24: 
25: - colony connectivity
26: - shipyards
27: - supply hubs
28: - direct usable hyperspace lanes
29: - empire logistics technology bonuses
30: - blockade state
31: 
32: Blocked colonies do not project fleet supply. Isolated colonies project weaker reach unless they have orbital support.
33: 
34: ## Penalties
35: 
36: Fleet supply penalties apply to combat fleets and troop transports:
37: 
38: | State | Attack | Defense | Travel Time | Invasion |
39: |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
40: | Supplied | 100% | 100% | 100% | 100% |
41: | Extended | 90% | 95% | 125% | 75% |
42: | Out of Supply | 75% | 80% | 160% | 0% |
43: 
44: Out-of-supply troop transports cannot invade.
45: 
46: ## UI Surfaces
47: 
48: Fleet supply is shown in:
49: 
50: - **Sector Map** system rows as projected supply for movement planning
51: - **System View** fleet roster and focused fleet status
52: - **Battle Reports** for both sides
53: - **Turn/log messages** when fleets arrive and in end-turn fleet supply summary
54: 
55: Labels stay literal for readability:
56: 
57: - `Supplied`
58: - `Extended`
59: - `Out of Supply`
60: 
61: ## Determinism Notes
62: 
63: - no wall-clock or OS randomness
64: - derived from seeded map/state only
65: - ordered collections or stable iteration required for any aggregate recalculation
66: - save migration re-derives fleet supply rather than trusting stale persisted values
67: 
68: ## Scope Limits
69: 
70: v1 does **not** add:
71: 
72: - per-ship fuel tracking
73: - manual supply convoy commands
74: - local stockpile simulation
75: - tactical combat fuel/ammo phases

(End of file - total 75 lines)
</content>

2: 
3: Diplomacy v3 adds deterministic treaties, diplomatic communications, first-contact introductions, and AI diplomatic actions.

5: ## Relationship states
6: 
7: - Unknown
8: - Contacted

25: 
26: ## Relationship and tension rules
27: 
28: - First contact creates status from faction diplomacy profile.
29: - Relationship drift remains deterministic and doctrine-aware.
30: - Border pressure and doctrine weights influence escalation/calming pace.
31: - Relationship updates emit `RelationshipStateChanged`.
32: - Status remains inspectable; no opaque random behavior.
33: 
34: ## Treaty types
35: 
36: Supported in v3:
37: 
38: - Non-Aggression Pact
39: - Truce (peace treaty)
40: 
41: Behavior:
42: 
43: - Non-Aggression Pact blocks war declaration while active.
44: - Truce ends war and blocks immediate redeclaration.
45: - Treaties have deterministic fixed durations.
46: - Expiry and cancellation emit events.
47: 
48: ## Communication system
49: 
50: `GameState.diplomacy_pending_communications` stores pending messages with deterministic IDs.
51: 
52: Communication types:
53: 
54: - FirstContact
55: - TreatyProposal
56: - TreatyAccepted
57: - TreatyRejected
58: - Warning
59: - TributeDemand
60: - PeaceOffer
61: - WarDeclaration

64: 
65: - `communication_id`
66: - sender/receiver
67: - turn
68: - type
69: - tone
70: - title/body
71: - available responses
72: - optional expiry
73: - optional treaty type
74:

77: - Same sender/receiver/type/treaty pending message is not duplicated before expiry.

80:

82: 
83: - Cooperative
84: - Formal
85: - Suspicious
86: - Threatening
87: - Hostile
88: - Desperate
89: - Triumphant

98: - Issue warnings (tense/hostile pressure posture)
99: - Demand tribute (high imperial/militarist hostility)
100: - Offer peace when losing wars

10: - **Militarist**: warship readiness, defenses, combat pressure.
11: - **Technologist**: science velocity, advanced capability timing.
12: - **Merchant**: credits, trade throughput, supply/logistics efficiency.
13: - **Isolationist**: internal stability, defensive posture, low-risk expansion.
14: - **Imperial**: coercive diplomacy, conquest tools, escalation posture.
15: - **Biologist**: food, housing, growth, adaptation priorities.
16: 
17: ## Faction-to-doctrine mapping
18: 
19: - **Ashveran Compact**: Industrialist + Isolationist
20: - **Luminal Traverse**: Explorer + Merchant + Expansionist
21: - **Sylvaran Accord**: Expansionist + Biologist
22: - **Thalori Exchange**: Merchant + Expansionist
23: - **Vorath Dominion**: Militarist + Imperial
24: - **Elarith Confluence**: Industrialist + Technologist + Isolationist
25: - **Terran Concord**: Explorer + Technologist + Merchant (lower aggression)
26: - **Terran Dominion**: Imperial + Militarist + Industrialist (higher aggression)
27: 
28: ## Decision areas affected
29: 
30: Doctrine weights bias deterministic scoring for:
31: 
32: - research plan and short research queue construction
33: - colony role and build queue priorities
34: - crisis reactions (food, housing, stability, blockades, local defense)
35: - shipyard and ship archetype production choices
36: - scouting/survey/colonization emphasis
37: - diplomacy drift and escalation pace
38: 
39: All actions remain rule-valid and use normal command/event paths.
40: 
41: ## Deterministic tie-breaking rules
42: 
43: AI decisions use stable ordering and explicit score ladders.
44: 
45: - Candidates are filtered first (valid/unlocked/not completed as applicable).
46: - Candidates are sorted deterministically with fixed keys (score + stable IDs/order fields).
47: - No stochastic behavior is used for doctrine choices.
48: - Same seed + same state + same faction identity yields same AI decisions.
49: 
50: ## Current limitations
51: 
52: - Doctrine reasoning is weighted heuristics, not long-horizon planning/search.
53: - No machine learning or hidden AI bonus resources.
54: - Diplomacy remains state-band drift, not full treaty negotiation.
55: - Tactical combat AI remains out of scope.
56: - Biologist is represented as doctrine axis for growth-oriented factions.
57: 
58: ## Future improvements
59: 
60: - richer doctrine-aware threat models for multi-front wars
61: - deeper doctrine hooks for future population/jobs systems
62: - broader doctrine-aware victory-path logic when victory framework expands
63: - optional developer-facing AI reasoning inspection tooling

(End of file - total 63 lines)
</content>

2:

4: 
5: ## Resource catalog
6: 
7: Ten resources:
8: 
9: - Quantum Crystals
10: - Reactive Isotopes
11: - Dark Matter
12: - Living Alloy
13: - Hyperfiber Organics
14: - Helium-3
15: - Psionic Spores
16: - Neutronium Deposits
17: - Antimatter Residue
18: - Precursor Datacores
19: 
20: Each resource defines:
21: 
22: - `resource_id`
23: - `name`
24: - `description`
25: - `rarity` (`Common`, `Uncommon`, `Rare`, `Legendary`)
26: - `category` (`Industrial`, `Energy`, `Military`, `Exotic`, `Biological`, `Precursor`)
27: - `discovery_requirements`
28: - `extraction_requirements`
29: - `tech_requirements`
30: - `strategic_effects`
31: - `trade_value`
32: - `future_hook_megaproject`
33: 
34: ## Placement philosophy
35: 
36: Generation is deterministic per galaxy seed and context, with asymmetry by:
37: 
38: - planet class
39: - star spectral class
40: - sector identity
41: - frontier distance from galactic center
42: - hazardous system signatures
43: - precursor signatures
44: - nebula-band signatures
45: 
46: Sectors can roll resource-poor or hotspot behavior. Rare and legendary resources have lower base weight and context-driven spikes.
47: 
48: ## Discovery rules
49: 
50: - Resources are hidden until survey completes.
51: - Discovery is also gated by resource-specific discovery techs.
52: - UI and Dispatch only surface discovered resources (no hidden-info leaks).
53: 
54: ## Extraction and control
55: 
56: Extraction requires:
57: 
58: - colony ownership/control
59: - required buildings/orbitals (resource-specific)
60: - required extraction tech (resource-specific)
61: - connected supply network
62: - no active blockade (for blockable resources)
63: 
64: `GameState.empire_resource_access` persists deterministic per-empire extracted counts and is recomputed from state each turn.
65: 
66: ## Strategic effects (v1)
67: 
68: v1 effects focus on clear, low-noise levers:
69: 
70: - empire-wide colony yield adjustments (industry/credits/science/food)
71: - limited research acceleration for precursor artifacts
72: - Helium-3 fleet maintenance relief
73: - advanced ship component gating by resource access
74: 
75: Effects are intentionally capped and non-explosive.
76: 
77: ## Tech integration
78: 
79: Resources use existing tech tree gates for:
80: 
81: - discovery visibility (survey/sensor-tier techs)
82: - extraction enablement (industry/orbital/precursor lanes)
83: - advanced ship component requirements
84: 
85: Early game remains playable with baseline designs and no rare resources.
86: 
87: ## AI valuation rules
88: 
89: AI uses deterministic resource-weighted scoring for:
90: 
91: - scout prospect targeting
92: - colonization target ranking
93: - wartime target selection (resource-rich enemy colony stars)
94: 
95: Doctrine weighting biases priorities:
96: 
97: - Industrialist: industrial assets
98: - Militarist: military assets
99: - Technologist: exotic/precursor assets
100: - Merchant: high trade-value assets
101: - Expansionist: energy/frontier assets
102: 
103: ## Galactic Dispatch integration
104: 
105: Resource discoveries emit dedicated events and can generate Dispatch headlines with rarity-scaled severity:
106: 
107: - Common: Notice
108: - Uncommon: Notable
109: - Rare: Urgent
110: - Legendary: Historic
111: 
112: ## UI/TUI integration
113: 
114: System and colony screens now show discovered resources with:
115: 
116: - rarity
117: - category
118: - trade value (system detail)
119: - extraction status (`active` / `offline`)
120: 
121: Diplomacy summary includes known empires’ strategic asset counts when contact exists.
122: 
123: Help overlay includes resource legend notes.
124: 
125: ## Save/load and determinism
126: 
127: - Save schema bumped to v34.
128: - Migration derives `empire_resource_access` deterministically.
129: - Placement, discovery visibility, extraction access, and AI targeting remain deterministic under fixed seed + command stream.
130: 
131: ## Intentional limitations (v1)
132: 
133: Not included in v1:
134: 
135: - manufacturing chains
136: - dynamic market pricing
137: - stock-market simulation
138: - crafting pipelines
139: - fuel logistics
140: - tactical harvesting minigames
141: - high-micromanagement resource spreadsheets
142: 
143: v1 prioritizes strategic clarity over simulation depth.

1: # Galactic Dispatch
2: 
3: Galactic Dispatch is a recurring in-universe news bulletin that surfaces important galaxy-wide events in an atmospheric, flavourful way. It improves strategic readability and game atmosphere without leaking hidden information or mutating game state.
4: 
5: ---
6: 
7: ## Feature Name
8: 
9: **Galactic Dispatch** — an in-universe signal intercept / intelligence briefing. Not modelled on any existing 4X franchise; all names, headlines, and presentation are original.
10: 
11: ---
12: 
13: ## Cadence
14: 
15: | Constant | Value | Meaning |
16: |---|---|---|
17: | `DISPATCH_CADENCE` | 5 | A dispatch is always generated every 5 turns |
18: | `DISPATCH_MAX_HISTORY` | 10 | At most 10 recent dispatches are retained in `GameState.galactic_dispatches` |
19: 
20: A dispatch is generated when `completed_turn % DISPATCH_CADENCE == 0`, where `completed_turn` is the value of `GameState::turn` **before** it is incremented. Because normal games start at `turn = 1`, the first in-game cadence dispatch is emitted when `state.turn` advances to a multiple of `DISPATCH_CADENCE + 1` (i.e. turns 5, 10, 15, …). The `completed_turn = 0` cadence used in unit tests reflects an initial state that starts before the first real game turn.
21: 
22: Off-cadence dispatches are only generated when at least one **Urgent** or **Historic** item is present (e.g. a blockade, invasion, or victory achievement).
23: 
24: ---
25: 
26: ## Data Model
27: 
28: ```
29: GalacticDispatch
30:   turn: u32                  — completed turn when the dispatch was generated
31:   title: String              — display title ("Galactic Dispatch — Turn N")
32:   items: Vec<DispatchItem>   — sorted, stable-ordered items
33: 
34: DispatchItem
35:   category: DispatchCategory
36:   severity: DispatchSeverity
37:   headline: String           — concise, atmospheric, original
38:   body: String               — one or two sentence expansion
39:   related_empire_id: Option<EmpireId>
40:   related_star_id: Option<StarId>
41:   related_planet_index: Option<usize>
42: ```
43: 
44: ---
45: 
46: ## Categories
47: 
48: | Variant | Covers |
49: |---|---|
50: | `Exploration` | System exploration, orbital surveys |
51: | `Colonization` | Colony founding (player and AI) |
52: | `Research` | Technology breakthroughs, research redirections |
53: | `Economy` | Credit deficits, food shortages |
54: | `Diplomacy` | First contact, relationship shifts |
55: | `War` | Fleet combat outcomes |
56: | `Blockades` | Blockade starts |
57: | `Invasions` | Planetary invasions (success and failure) |
58: | `Trade` | Colony isolation / supply network disruption |
59: | `VictoryRace` | Victory-path progress milestones, winner |
60: | `MinorFactions` | Reserved for future minor faction contacts |
61: 
62: ---
63: 
64: ## Severity Levels
65: 
66: | Variant | Marker | Style | When used |
67: |---|---|---|---|
68: | `Notice` | `[·]` | Muted | Routine exploration, AI research redirections |
69: | `Notable` | `[»]` | Title | Colonization, first contact, minor war, food shortage |
70: | `Urgent` | `[!!]` | Error (red) | Blockades, credit deficit, invasion attempts |
71: | `Historic` | `[★★]` | Accent | Ancient ruins, high-progress victory milestones (≥80 %), victories, invasion conquests |
72: 
73: ---
74: 
75: ## Generation Sources
76: 
77: The dispatch is derived from the event stream emitted during `process_end_turn`. The following `Event` variants map to dispatch items:
78: 
79: | Event | Category | Severity |
80: |---|---|---|
81: | `SystemExplored` | Exploration | Notice |
82: | `PlanetSurveyCompleted` | Exploration | Notice |
83: | `AncientRuinsDiscovered` | Research | Historic |
84: | `ColonizationCompleted` | Colonization | Notable |
85: | `AiColonized` | Colonization | Notable (or vague if empire unknown) |
86: | `ResearchCompleted` (player) | Research | Notable |
87: | `AiResearchSelected` | Research | Notice (if empire known) |
88: | `CombatResolved` | War | Urgent/Notable depending on player involvement |
89: | `BlockadeStarted` | Blockades | Urgent |
90: | `InvasionSucceeded` | Invasions | Historic |
91: | `InvasionFailed` | Invasions | Notable |
92: | `FoodShortage` (player) | Economy | Urgent |
93: | `EconomySummary` with deficit (player) | Economy | Notable |
94: | `ColonyIsolated` (player colony) | Trade | Notable |
95: | `FirstContact` | Diplomacy | Notable |
96: | `VictoryProgressMilestone` | VictoryRace | Notable (or Historic if ≥80 %) |
97: | `VictoryAchieved` | VictoryRace | Historic |
98: 
99: Dispatches do not generate random events — they only reflect what actually happened this turn.
100: 
101: ---
102: 
103: ## Public Information Rules
104: 
105: Dispatch content is filtered to avoid leaking hidden state:
106: 
107: 1. **Unknown empires**: if the player has not made contact with an empire (`RelationshipStatus::Unknown` or absent from `diplomacy`), that empire's name and ID are withheld. Vague wording is used instead:
108:    - "Unknown Forces Establish Remote Colony"
109:    - "Unidentified Fleet Engages Forces Near [star]"
110:    - "Unidentified Fleet Blockades Contested Colony"
111: 
112: 2. **Unsurveyed planets**: planet specials and strategic resources are never referenced in dispatch text until the planet has been surveyed.
113: 
114: 3. **Unseen stars**: system exploration events are only surfaced when the player's own fleet explored them (event is already player-scoped). AI-explored stars are not reported as exploration events.
115: 
116: 4. **AI combat**: if the player is not involved in combat and neither fleet's empire is known, the combat event is skipped entirely.
117: 
118: ---
119: 
120: ## Item Ordering (Determinism)
121: 
122: Items are sorted by a composite key:
123: 
124: 1. Severity descending (Historic → Urgent → Notable → Notice)
125: 2. Category ascending (enum declaration order, mapped to u8)
126: 3. Headline ascending (lexicographic)
127: 
128: This produces a stable, deterministic order regardless of event insertion order or BTreeMap iteration. Same events + same state always produce identical dispatch output.
129: 
130: ---
131: 
132: ## Deduplication
133: 
134: Multiple events of the same type in one turn are collapsed:
135: - Multiple `SystemExplored` events → one Exploration item ("Survey Crews Chart New Frontier Worlds")
136: - Multiple `PlanetSurveyCompleted` events → one Exploration item
137: 
138: This is achieved via a `BTreeSet<(DispatchCategory, String)>` deduplication set.
139: 
140: ---
141: 
142: ## Examples
143: 
144: ```
145: ╔══════════════════════════════════════════╗
146: ║       ◈ GALACTIC DISPATCH ◈              ║
147: ║  Turn 5  ·  Dispatch 1/1                 ║
148: ║──────────────────────────────────────────║
149: ║ [★★] [RESEARCH]                          ║
150: ║  Ancient Ruins Discovered —              ║
151: ║  Archaeological Teams Mobilize           ║
152: ║   Excavations begun at Keth Prime.       ║
153: ║                                          ║
154: ║ [»]  [COLONIZATION]                      ║
155: ║  Colonists Establish Foothold in         ║
156: ║  Vela System                             ║
157: ║   A colonial charter has been issued     ║
158: ║   for Vela II.                           ║
159: ║──────────────────────────────────────────║
160: ║  ← prev / → next   Esc to close         ║
161: ╚══════════════════════════════════════════╝
162: ```
163: 
164: ---
165: 
166: ## TUI Interaction
167: 
168: | Key / Command | Action |
169: |---|---|
170: | `N` (global, in-game) | Open latest Galactic Dispatch |
171: | `:dispatch` | Open latest Galactic Dispatch |
172: | `:news` | Alias for `:dispatch` |
173: | `←` / `h` | Cycle to previous dispatch in history |
174: | `→` / `l` | Cycle to next dispatch in history |
175: | `Esc` / `N` / `n` | Close dispatch overlay |
176: 
177: The dispatch overlay is shown automatically when a new dispatch is generated at the end of a turn.
178: 
179: ---
180: 
181: ## Persistence (Save/Load)
182: 
183: `galactic_dispatches` is stored in `GameState` as a `VecDeque<GalacticDispatch>`. It is serialised via serde (behind the `serde` feature flag on `game_core`). Old saves (schema ≤ 28) load with an empty history via `#[serde(default)]`.
184: 
185: Save schema version: **29** (introduced with Galactic Dispatch v1).
186: 
187: ---
188: 
189: ## Determinism and Replay
190: 
191: - `generate_dispatch` takes only `completed_turn`, the event slice, and a shared reference to `GameState`. It uses no RNG and no wall-clock logic.
192: - Same seed + same command log → same events → same dispatches.
193: - `galactic_dispatches` is included in `GameState`'s manual `PartialEq` implementation, so equality checks (e.g. in save-load round-trip tests) compare dispatch history along with all other game state.
194: 
195: ---
196: 
197: ## Future Hooks
198: 
199: - **Minor faction sightings**: `MinorFactions` category is reserved for when minor independent factions are introduced.
200: - **Reduced-interruptions mode**: a future `reduced_interruptions` flag in UI settings can suppress automatic dispatch opening.
201: - **Dispatch filtering by category**: the TUI modal could gain a category filter.
202: - **Clickable context links**: headlines with `related_star_id` could eventually jump to that system.
203: - **Urgent off-cadence dispatch**: the off-cadence Urgent/Historic rule is already implemented; future "galactic crisis" events can piggyback on it.

(End of file - total 203 lines)
</content>

1: # Balance and Pacing — v1
2: 
3: This document describes the pacing goals, key formulas, scaling assumptions, intended game
4: phases, AI balance philosophy, and known limitations for FARSPACE's first balance pass.
5: 
6: ---
7: 
8: ## Pacing Goals
9: 
10: ### Early Game (Turns 1–15)
11: 
12: - Exploration and survey should matter immediately.
13: - First research unlock should arrive within **10–15 turns** on a standard start.
14: - First scout returns survey data within 5–10 turns.
15: - Colony decisions (role, build priority) should feel meaningful from turn 1.
16: - Players should not become economically trapped under normal play.
17: - First diplomatic contacts occur naturally (AI explores toward player territory).
18: - Military conflict should not occur before turn 20 (the AI combat-fleet dispatch
19:   is gated behind `turn >= 20`).
20: 
21: ### Mid Game (Turns 15–80)
22: 
23: - First colonisation wave completes (Survey Drones + Habitat Seeding + Colony Ship built).
24: - Competing borders and diplomacy emerge by turn 40–60.
25: - Shipyards and fleet composition begin to matter.
26: - AI empires diverge strategically by doctrine.
27: - Multiple viable strategic paths are open:
28:   - Military (Dominion)
29:   - Economic (Prosperity)
30:   - Scientific (Ascendancy)
31:   - Expansionist (Discovery)
32:   - Diplomatic (Unity)
33: 
34: ### Late Game (Turns 80+)
35: 
36: - Victory pressure becomes visible (at least one path reaches ≥50% progress).
37: - Major wars and economic advantages shape the map.
38: - Advanced techs (T4–T6) feel impactful.
39: - Economy scales without exponential collapse.
40: 
41: ---
42: 
43: ## Major Formulas
44: 
45: ### Colony Production (Industry)
46: 
47: ```
48: industry = population + (FabricationYard_count × 2) + stability_modifier + role_modifier
49: stability_modifier = (stability − 100) / 10      # 0 at neutral-100; negative below 100
50: ```
51: 
52: **v1 fix**: The build-queue production pool now uses `colony_yield.industry` (scaled with
53: population and buildings) instead of the stale `colony.production` field (which was
54: initialised to 10 and never updated). This makes production speed scale with colony growth.
55: 
56: ```
57: effective_production = max(colony_yield.industry, colony.production)  // legacy floor
58: production_pool = accumulated_production + effective_production + ship_role_bonus
59: ```
60: 
61: ### Colony Yields per Turn
62: 
63: ```
64: credits  = (industry × prod_pct / 100) + role_flat + tech_bonus_per_colony
65: science  = (industry × research_pct / 100) + ScienceNexus_bonus + planet_bonus + role_flat + tech_bonus
66: food     = population + (AquacultureBay_count × population) + planet_bonus + role_flat
67: food_consumed = population
68: ```
69: 
70: Starting colony (pop=10, no buildings, 50/50 split):
71: 
72: | Resource | Per-Turn |
73: |----------|----------|
74: | Production | 10 |
75: | Credits | 5 |
76: | Science | 5 |
77: 
78: ### Research Pacing
79: 
80: Science per turn scales with `colony.industry × research_pct / 100`. With a default 50/50
81: focus and population 10:
82: 
83: | Tech | Cost | Turns to complete (5 sci/turn) |
84: |------|------|---------------------------------|
85: | Void Propulsion (T1) | 40 | 8 |
86: | Neutrino Sensors (T1) | 50 | 10 |
87: | Survey Drones (T2) | 75 | 15 |
88: | Habitat Seeding (T1) | 65 | 13 |
89: | Colonial Logistics (T2) | 120 | 24 |
90: | Orbital Engineering (T2) | 150 | 30 |
91: 
92: Tech costs were reduced **15–25% for T1** and **~20% for critical T2 gates** (Survey Drones,
93: Drift Mapping) to ensure the first research rewards arrive within the target window.
94: 
95: ### Population Growth
96: 
97: ```
98: growth_tick = every POP_GROWTH_PERIOD_TURNS turns where (turn + colony_id) % period == 0
99: conditions  = not blockaded
100:             AND stability >= MIN_STABILITY_FOR_POP_GROWTH
101:             AND empire food >= 0
102:             AND housing_deficit == 0
103:             AND food >= food_consumed
104: ```
105: 
106: | Constant | v0 | v1 | Reason |
107: |----------|----|----|--------|
108: | `POP_GROWTH_PERIOD_TURNS` | 12 | 10 | Faster early growth |
109: | `MIN_STABILITY_FOR_POP_GROWTH` | 90 | 80 | More forgiving threshold |
110: 
111: ### Stability Penalties (per turn)
112: 
113: | Condition | Penalty |
114: |-----------|---------|
115: | Colony isolated (not connected) | −5 |
116: | Colony blockaded | **−8** (was −5) |
117: | Housing deficit | −`min(deficit, 10)` |
118: | Unemployed population | −`min(unemployed, 5)` |
119: | Isolated + food deficit | −`min(deficit, 5)` |
120: 
121: Blockade penalty was raised from 5 → 8 so blockades require a strategic response within
122: roughly 12 turns before severe destabilisation.
123: 
124: ### Isolation / Blockade Yield Penalty
125: 
126: Isolated and blockaded colonies both receive:
127: ```
128: credits' = credits × 50 / 100
129: science' = science × 50 / 100
130: food'    = 0   (no food export while cut off)
131: ```
132: 
133: ### Fleet Maintenance
134: 
135: ```
136: maintenance_per_fleet = kind.maintenance_cost() + empire_modifier
137: total_maintenance = Σ max(0, maintenance_per_fleet) for all empire fleets
138: ```
139: 
140: Fleet maintenance is deducted from empire credits each turn after colony production.
141: A soft-cap constant `FLEET_MAINTENANCE_CREDIT_CAP_PER_EMPIRE = 50` is defined in
142: `balance.rs` for future use (doubled upkeep above the cap to deter fleet spam).
143: 
144: ### Invasion
145: 
146: ```
147: invasion_strength = troop_transports × (TROOP_TRANSPORT_INVASION_STRENGTH + empire_bonus)
148:                   = troop_transports × (12 + empire_bonus)
149: ```
150: 
151: | Constant | v0 | v1 | Reason |
152: |----------|----|----|--------|
153: | `CAPTURED_UNREST_STABILITY` | 40 | 45 | Captured worlds slightly less crippled |
154: 
155: ### Fleet Travel
156: 
157: ```
158: travel_turns = max(1, ceil(distance / FLEET_TRAVEL_SPEED))
159:              = max(1, ceil(distance / 500.0))
160: 
161: lane_turns   = max(1, ceil(base_turns / HYPERSPACE_TRAVEL_DIVISOR))
162:              = max(1, ceil(base_turns / 2))
163: ```
164: 
165: Stars are generated in `−500..=500` on each axis; max distance ≈ 1414 units:
166: 
167: | Distance | Base turns | Lane turns |
168: |----------|-----------|------------|
169: | ≤ 500 | 1 | 1 |
170: | ≤ 1000 | 2 | 1 |
171: | > 1000 | 3 | 2 |
172: 
173: ---
174: 
175: ## Scaling Assumptions
176: 
177: 1. **Production scales with population.** After the v1 fix, a colony at pop 20 produces
178:    roughly twice the production output of a pop-10 colony (before buildings).
179: 
180: 2. **FabricationYard adds +2 industry.** Three yards on a pop-10 colony raise industry from
181:    10 to 16 (+60%), making early building investment highly rewarding.
182: 
183: 3. **Science/credits scale linearly** with industry until late-game tech bonuses compound.
184:    No exponential growth is intended; per-colony tech yield bonuses are small flat amounts.
185: 
186: 4. **Fleet maintenance acts as a soft fleet-count cap.** Each fleet costs 1–4 credits/turn;
187:    an empire earning 15–20 credits/turn can support roughly 4–10 fleets before maintenance
188:    becomes strategically significant.
189: 
190: 5. **Victory progress scales with empire breadth.** Dominion requires controlling 60% of
191:    colonised systems; Discovery requires 80% of stars explored + 70% of planets surveyed.
192:    Neither is achievable purely by turtling.
193: 
194: ---
195: 
196: ## Intended Game Phases
197: 
198: | Phase | Turns | Key events |
199: |-------|-------|-----------|
200: | Exploration | 1–15 | First tech, scouts explore nearby stars |
201: | Early Expansion | 15–40 | Survey Drones → coloniser built → first new colony |
202: | Border Contact | 40–60 | AI contact, diplomacy established |
203: | Economic Divergence | 60–80 | Shipyards built, fleet doctrine matters |
204: | Late-Game Pressure | 80+ | War, victory paths visible, advanced techs |
205: 
206: ---
207: 
208: ## AI Balance Philosophy
209: 
210: ### Doctrine-Driven Priorities
211: 
212: AI empires choose research and builds based on weighted doctrine axes:
213: 
214: | Doctrine | Research bias | Build bias |
215: |----------|--------------|-----------|
216: | Explorer | Exploration, Survey | Scout, Science Ship |
217: | Expansionist | Colonisation, Biology | Colony Ship, Colony Ark |
218: | Industrialist | Engineering | Fabrication Yard, Shipyard |
219: | Militarist | Military | Combat ships |
220: | Imperial | Military + Society | Combat ships, troop transports |
221: | Merchant | Economy, Logistics | Fabrication Yard |
222: | Technologist | Engineering, Society | Science Nexus |
223: | Biologist | Biology | Aquaculture Bay |
224: | Isolationist | Society, Stability | Stability buildings |
225: 
226: ### AI Combat (v1)
227: 
228: AI empires now dispatch idle combat fleets toward enemy colonies when at war:
229: 
230: - Activates only at `turn >= 20` (prevents immediate early aggression).
231: - Only combat fleet kinds (EscortFrigate, MissileFrigate, Destroyer, PatrolCorvette) are
232:   dispatched; scouts and colonisers are not used for war.
233: - Target is the nearest player colony by squared distance.
234: - All dispatch decisions are deterministic: fleets sorted by `FleetId`, targets sorted by
235:   `StarId`.
236: 
237: ### AI Limitations in v1
238: 
239: - The AI does not declare war proactively (only the player can declare war).
240: - The AI does not evaluate peace opportunities or sue for peace.
241: - The AI does not use blockades strategically (fleet movement to blockade positions is
242:   reactive, not planned).
243: - The AI does not coordinate multiple fleets for combined arms.
244: - Research plan length is short (2–4 techs); it does not plan long tech chains.
245: 
246: ---
247: 
248: ## Victory Conditions (Default)
249: 
250: | Path | Conditions |
251: |------|------------|
252: | Dominion | Control ≥60% of all colonised systems |
253: | Ascendancy | Complete ≥4 of 6 designated victory technologies |
254: | Prosperity | Pop ≥40, Credits ≥300, ≥4 connected colonies, avg stability ≥95, food surplus ≥0 |
255: | Discovery | 80% stars explored, 70% planets surveyed, Hyperspace Cartography + Sector Cartography |
256: | Unity | Contact ≥2 empires, ≥2 non-war relations, ≥3 connected colonies |
257: 
258: All paths are enabled by default except Unity (which requires non-war diplomatic investment).
259: 
260: ---
261: 
262: ## Known Balance Risks and Future Work
263: 
264: ### Short-term
265: 
266: - **Prosperity victory** may be easier than intended because the stability threshold (≥95)
267:   can be maintained by a turtling player who avoids expansion. Consider adding a minimum
268:   empire-size requirement.
269: - **Discovery victory** requires 80% star exploration; on small maps this is achievable
270:   early, on large maps it may be too hard. Consider making the threshold map-size-aware.
271: - **Fleet maintenance** soft cap (`FLEET_MAINTENANCE_CREDIT_CAP_PER_EMPIRE = 50`) is
272:   defined but **not yet wired into the engine**. Without it, wealthy empires can spam cheap
273:   scouts to maintain map presence at low cost.
274: - **AI never declares war**: players who prefer defence can survive indefinitely without
275:   meaningful military threat beyond blocking AI expansion.
276: 
277: ### Mid-term
278: 
279: - Colony growth gating on `empire.food >= 0` creates a hard cliff: any food deficit halts
280:   growth empire-wide regardless of which colony is deficient. Consider per-colony food
281:   accounting.
282: - Pop growth at period 10 with pop=10 means a colony reaches pop=15 after ~50 turns if
283:   conditions are met continuously. This may still feel slow for wide-expansion strategies.
284: - Research scaling is flat (no diminishing returns); a player or AI that focuses heavily on
285:   science buildings can compress mid-game research significantly.
286: 
287: ### Long-term (requires new features)
288: 
289: - **Megastructures** (future): tech hooks defined (`future_hook: true`); balance TBD.
290: - **Crises** (future): no crisis system yet; late-game may feel unchallenging once dominant.
291: - **Advanced diplomacy** (future): treaties, trade routes, and alliance mechanics would give
292:   Unity and Prosperity paths more strategic depth.
293: - **Custom ship design** (future): current ship archetypes provide basic fleet diversity but
294:   do not allow mid-game design adaptation.
295: - **Espionage** (future): `TechTag::EspionageFuture` is defined; no implementation yet.
296: 
297: ---
298: 
299: ## Centralized Balance Constants
300: 
301: All numeric tuning values live in `crates/game_core/src/balance.rs`. See that file for
302: inline documentation of each constant's purpose and intended effect.
303: 
304: Key constants:
305: 
306: ```rust
307: POP_GROWTH_PERIOD_TURNS             = 10   // turns between growth ticks
308: MIN_STABILITY_FOR_POP_GROWTH        = 80   // stability floor for growth
309: BLOCKADED_STABILITY_PENALTY         = 8    // per-turn stability loss under blockade
310: ISOLATED_YIELD_PERCENT              = 50   // % yield retained while isolated
311: TROOP_TRANSPORT_INVASION_STRENGTH   = 12   // strength per troop transport
312: CAPTURED_UNREST_STABILITY           = 45   // stability after colony capture
313: BORDER_TENSION_DISTANCE_SQ          = 40_000 // ~200 map units: routine tension
314: SEVERE_BORDER_TENSION_DISTANCE_SQ   = 12_000 // ~110 map units: severe tension
315: FLEET_TRAVEL_SPEED                  = 500.0  // map units per turn
316: HYPERSPACE_TRAVEL_DIVISOR           = 2      // lane speed multiplier (÷2)
317: FLEET_MAINTENANCE_CREDIT_CAP_PER_EMPIRE = 50 // reserved, not yet active
318: ```

(End of file - total 318 lines)
</content>

# Balance and Pacing — v1

This document describes the pacing goals, key formulas, scaling assumptions, intended game
phases, AI balance philosophy, and known limitations for FARSPACE's first balance pass.

---

## Pacing Goals

### Early Game (Turns 1–15)

- Exploration and survey should matter immediately.
- First research unlock should arrive within **10–15 turns** on a standard start.
- First scout returns survey data within 5–10 turns.
- Colony decisions (role, build priority) should feel meaningful from turn 1.
- Players should not become economically trapped under normal play.
- First diplomatic contacts occur naturally (AI explores toward player territory).
- Military conflict should not occur before turn 20 (the AI combat-fleet dispatch
  is gated behind `turn >= 20`).

1: # Internal Stability and Unrest v1
2: 
3: ## Goals
4: 
5: - slow conquest and overexpansion snowball
6: - make frontier and occupied colonies strategic liabilities
7: - add internal pressure without deep political simulation
8: - keep model deterministic and explainable
9: 
10: ## Unrest States
11: 
12: Colony order now resolves into one of four deterministic states:
13: 
14: - `Calm`
15: - `Strained`
16: - `Unrest`
17: - `Revolt Risk`
18: 
19: State is derived from a weighted unrest score each turn and cached in `GameState.colony_unrest` for UI/reporting.
20: 
21: ## Unrest Contributors
22: 
23: Per-colony contributors:
24: 
25: - food shortage
26: - housing shortage
27: - low stability bands
28: - recent conquest (decays over fixed turn window)
29: - blockade
30: - isolated / out-of-supply colony
31: - empire war exhaustion pressure
32: - empire overextension pressure (colony count above threshold)
33: 
34: ## Empire-Level Pressure
35: 
36: Per-empire unrest pressure is deterministic:
37: 
38: - `war_exhaustion`: active war relation present
39: - `overextension`: colony count above `OVEREXTENSION_COLONY_THRESHOLD`
40: 
41: These pressures are applied uniformly to owned colonies as unrest contributors.
42: 
43: ## Penalties
44: 
45: Unrest states apply deterministic colony penalties:
46: 
47: - reduced production throughput
48: - reduced credits/science output
49: - increased colony maintenance
50: - increased rebellion risk basis points (`colony_rebellion_risk_bp`) as future hook
51: 
52: Note: build throughput is based on colony-local industry (then unrest penalty), while empire/resource flat economic bonuses affect economy outputs only and do not directly accelerate build-pool accumulation.
53: 
54: No rebellion mechanics are executed in v1.
55: 
56: ## Conquest Handling
57: 
58: On successful invasion:
59: 
60: - captured colony stability is set to `CAPTURED_UNREST_STABILITY`
61: - conquest turn is recorded in `colony_recent_conquest_turn`
62: - colony starts at least in severe unrest pressure path (`Revolt Risk` cache seed)
63: 
64: Recent-conquest pressure decays over a fixed window (`CONQUEST_UNREST_TURNS`).
65: 
66: ## Recovery
67: 
68: Unrest is recomputed every turn from current conditions.
69: If shortages, blockade, war pressure, or overextension ease, colonies naturally recover toward `Calm`.
70: 
71: ## Determinism
72: 
73: - no global RNG or wall-clock logic
74: - sorted colony iteration preserved for stable event order
75: - unrest transitions emitted via deterministic `ColonyUnrestChanged` events
76: - save/load persists unrest caches and conquest timestamps
77: 
78: ## UI Surfaces
79: 
80: Unrest is surfaced in:
81: 
82: - Colony screen (state, causes, rebellion risk)
83: - System view colony status labels
84: - Empire Overview rows and summary (unrest highlight)
85: - Turn summary report (unrest worsened / revolt-risk counts)
86: - Galactic Dispatch (major unrest escalation items)
87: - Help overlay notes
88: 
89: ## Scope Limits
90: 
91: Explicitly out of scope in v1:
92: 
93: - political factions
94: - ideology trees
95: - rebellions and civil wars
96: - governors and migration politics
97: - deep approval simulation

(End of file - total 97 lines)
</content>

1: # FARSPACE TUI Style Guide
2: 
3: Practical rules for keeping every screen part of one coherent product. When in
4: doubt, reuse a shared helper instead of writing one-off style code.
5: 
6: Source of cinematic intent: `ux-splash-screen.md`. This document covers the
7: working screens.
8: 
9: ---
10: 
11: ## Color philosophy
12: 
13: - **Use semantic `Theme` roles, never raw `Color::Rgb` in screens.** Screens
14:   call roles like `Theme::title_style()`, `accent_style()`, `warning_style()`,
15:   `faction_color()`, `bright_star()`. RGB literals live only in `theme/` and
16:   `components/`.
17: - Roles carry meaning, not just a hue: `error`/`danger` = blocking or hostile,
18:   `warning` = deficit or caution, `success` = surplus or friendly, `accent` =
19:   interactive/selected, `muted` = secondary or hidden information.
20: - The palette degrades through three modes (`theme/capability.rs`):
21:   `TrueColor → Ansi256 → Mono`. RGB-specific roles branch on
22:   `Theme::color_mode()`; named-ANSI roles map naturally in all modes.
23: - Faction identity comes from `Theme::faction_color` (foreground) and
24:   `faction_territory_color` (map fill). Do not invent per-screen faction hues.
25: 
26: ## Border usage
27: 
28: - `page_block(title)` — the focused outer frame of a full screen.
29: - `panel_block(title, focused)` — a sub-panel; pass `focused` to drive the
30:   border between `focused_border_style` and `dim_border_style`.
31: - `quiet_panel_block(title)` — a non-interactive companion panel.
32: - All blocks use the `ROUNDED` border set. Do not hand-roll `Block::default()`
33:   with ad-hoc borders except for genuine error/modal surfaces (e.g. the
34:   unavailable-screen fallback uses an error border deliberately).
35: - One focused border per screen at a time. The focused panel signals where
36:   keyboard input goes.
37: 
38: ## Footer rules
39: 
40: - Footers come from `components/footer.rs` — one arm per `Screen`.
41: - Keep hints **restrained: ~4–7 core entries.** Prefer the primary action,
42:   navigation, end-turn, `?` Help, and back/quit. Secondary commands live in the
43:   `?` help overlay, not the footer.
44: - Format is `Key Label │ Key Label …`; the component wraps cleanly on narrow
45:   terminals. Avoid command dumps.
46: - Every interactive screen exposes `?` Help in its footer.
47: - Do not duplicate a control in both a panel body and the footer. If body copy
48:   already teaches the keys, drop them from the footer.
49: 
50: ## Selection / focus state rules
51: 
52: - **Selection must never be color-only.** Every selectable row carries a glyph
53:   marker plus a style change: list rows use `▶`/`>` prefixes, map/planet
54:   cursors use a distinct glyph (`•` vs `·`). The marker keeps selection legible
55:   in Mono mode and for color-blind users.
56: - Status that matters carries a symbol too, not just a hue — e.g. diplomacy
57:   relationships use `⚠` Hostile / `⚔` War / `●` Contacted alongside color.
58: - Selected rows use `Theme::highlight_style()` (bold + inverted) on top of the
59:   marker, never instead of it.
60: 
61: ## Resize expectations
62: 
63: - Validate at `80x24`, `100x30`, `120x36`, `160x44`. `80x24` is the floor.
64: - Use `Constraint`-based layouts from `layout.rs` (`compose_layout`,
65:   `split_sidebar_main`, `split_main_detail`). Never compute fixed offsets that
66:   assume a width.
67: - At small sizes: keep the footer visible, never clip titles, never overlap
68:   panels. Collapse secondary sections (long descriptions, emblem columns)
69:   first; preserve the list + selected-detail and the functional controls.
70: - Wide sizes earn richer detail (sidebar + detail, emblem art), not bigger fonts
71:   of the same content.
72: 
73: ## Accessibility expectations
74: 
75: - Important state is conveyed by **glyph/shape + text**, not color alone.
76: - Warnings and errors include a symbol or word, never a bare colored number.
77: - Muted/disabled text must stay readable (use `muted_style`, not near-bg hues).
78: - Monochrome fallback must remain usable: prefer named ANSI roles for text, and
79:   keep `SplashPalette::for_mode(Mono)` grayscale-only.
80: 
81: ## When to use emblems
82: 
83: - Emblems (`components/emblem.rs`) are for **identity moments**: empire select,
84:   the diplomacy detail panel, setup. They answer "who is this faction?"
85: - Resolve via `EmpireEmblem::from_empire_index` / `resolve_empire_emblem*`.
86:   Render with `render_empire_emblem`, which self-sizes and drops its border at
87:   small areas.
88: - Do not scatter emblems into dense data screens (research, colony build lists)
89:   where they compete with information.
90: 
91: ## When *not* to use decorative panels
92: 
93: - Don't wrap every value in its own bordered box. Borders cost two rows/columns
94:   and fragment scanning. Group related data under a `section_heading` inside one
95:   panel instead.
96: - No telemetry-style widgets or fake status meters. A meter (`meter_line`) must
97:   reflect real game state.
98: - Keep composition calm and spacious. Decoration serves hierarchy; if it does
99:   not help the player read the screen, leave it out.

(End of file - total 99 lines)
</content>

1: # Espionage and Intelligence Lite v1
2: 
3: Espionage and Intelligence Lite v1 adds deterministic rival-knowledge progression without spy units, random mission chains, or per-agent micromanagement.
4: 
5: ## Goals
6: 
7: - make diplomacy, war, and scouting carry information value
8: - keep intel deterministic and explainable
9: - reveal rival data in layers instead of all-at-once omniscience
10: - leave hooks for later sabotage and research theft slices
11: 
12: ## Intel levels
13: 
14: Each foreign empire resolves to one of five player-facing intel levels:
15: 
16: - **Unknown** — no contact, no verified rival detail
17: - **Contacted** — diplomatic stance known, richer data still hidden
18: - **Basic** — colony count and coarse fleet strength visible
19: - **Informed** — tech tier and economy snapshot visible, fleet detail improves
20: - **Deep** — strategic-resource access visible
21: 
22: ## Passive intel gain
23: 
24: Passive intel progresses every end turn for contacted empires.
25: 
26: Deterministic sources:
27: 
28: - contact itself
29: - nearby fleet or colony presence
30: - survey / sensor technology
31: - active treaties
32: 
33: No wall-clock logic. No global RNG. Stable empire ordering preserved with ordered collections.
34: 
35: ## Active intel action
36: 
37: v1 adds one direct action:
38: 
39: - **Gather Intelligence** — deterministic, immediate point gain, once per target per turn
40: 
41: Future hooks are surfaced as placeholders only:
42: 
43: - **Sabotage Production**
44: - **Steal Research**
45: 
46: They intentionally do not resolve real effects in Lite v1.
47: 
48: ## Visibility rules
49: 
50: Intel level controls rival visibility in diplomacy, dispatch, logs, and system views:
51: 
52: - colony count: Basic+
53: - fleet strength: Basic+
54: - tech level: Informed+
55: - economy summary: Informed+
56: - diplomatic stance: Contacted+
57: - strategic resources: Deep
58: 
59: Foreign colony and fleet panels avoid leaking unrevealed values before the required intel level is reached.
60: 
61: ## UI surfaces
62: 
63: - Diplomacy screen shows intel level and gated empire detail
64: - System screen hides foreign colony and fleet detail until intel improves
65: - Turn Report counts intel gains
66: - Help overlay documents intel controls
67: - Galactic Dispatch redacts rival colonization / research items until the required intel level is reached
68: 
69: ## Advisor
70: 
71: Advisor now warns when contacted empires remain below informed intel and points player toward the diplomacy screen.
72: 
73: ## Save/load
74: 
75: - `GameState.empire_intel` persists current intel progress
76: - save schema bumped to v38
77: - v37 → v38 seeds contacted empires with baseline intel on load
78: 
79: ## Scope limits
80: 
81: Not included in v1:
82: 
83: - spy agents
84: - mission chains
85: - counterintelligence systems
86: - assassinations, coups, or procedural espionage event spam
87: - random mission outcomes

1: //! Centralized balance constants for FARSPACE.
2: //!
3: //! This module is the **single source of truth** for every numeric value that
4: //! affects game pacing, economic output, combat resolution, and diplomatic
5: //! triggers.  All constants are `pub` so that other crates (e.g. the TUI) can
6: //! display tuning information to the player, and so integration tests can
7: //! assert on them directly.
8: //!
9: //! # Pacing Intent
10: //!
11: //! The values here were tuned for the following target experience:
12: //!
13: //! * **Turns 1–15** — Exploration and first research unlocks.  The player
14: //!   should complete at least one T1 tech and see their first scout return
15: //!   data within 15 turns.
16: //! * **Turns 15–40** — First colonisation wave.  Survey Drones gating
17: //!   colonisation is deliberately cheap so this window feels achievable.
18: //! * **Turns 40–80** — Border contact with AI, early skirmishes.  Blockades
19: //!   and stability pressure start to shape strategic decisions.
20: //! * **Turns 80+** — Mid-game wars and economic differentiation.
21: //!
22: //! # Changing Constants
23: //!
24: //! Prefer modifying this file over hard-coding values anywhere else.  Every
25: //! constant documents its intended effect so reviewers can evaluate trade-offs
26: //! without hunting through the engine code.
27: 
28: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
29: // Research pacing
30: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
31: 
32: /// Multiplier applied to T1 tech costs.  Set to 1 (no scaling) so the raw
33: /// `TechRecord::cost` values drive pacing directly.
34: ///
35: /// **Currently unused in engine code** — serves as a reference/documentation
36: /// value capturing the design decision that cost scaling is achieved by editing
37: /// `TechRecord::cost` entries directly rather than via a runtime multiplier.
38: pub const EARLY_TECH_COST_MULTIPLIER: i64 = 1;
39: 
40: /// Base science output per population unit contributed by the yield model.
41: ///
42: /// Increasing this shortens the research ladder; decreasing it stretches it.
43: ///
44: /// **Currently unused in engine code** — documents the implicit 1:1 ratio
45: /// between a colony's population count and its base science contribution before
46: /// building/role modifiers are applied (see `yield_model::calculate_yield`).
47: pub const BASE_SCIENCE_PER_POP: i64 = 1;
48: 
49: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
50: // Colony growth
51: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
52: 
53: /// Number of turns between automatic population growth ticks.
54: ///
55: /// **Changed from 12 → 10** to give a slightly faster early-game growth feel
56: /// and ensure colonies feel alive within the first two dozen turns.
57: pub const POP_GROWTH_PERIOD_TURNS: u32 = 10;
58: 
59: /// Minimum colony stability required for population to grow.
60: ///
61: /// **Changed from 90 → 80** to be slightly more forgiving; colonies under
62: /// mild pressure (housing deficit or minor food issues) can still grow.
63: pub const MIN_STABILITY_FOR_POP_GROWTH: u8 = 80;
64: 
65: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
66: // Economic penalties
67: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
68: 
69: /// Yield percentage retained by an isolated (disconnected) colony.
70: ///
71: /// Credits and science are multiplied by this value divided by 100.
72: /// Food is zeroed out entirely regardless of this setting.
73: pub const ISOLATED_YIELD_PERCENT: i64 = 50;
74: 
75: /// Stability lost per turn while a colony is isolated (not connected to the
76: /// empire supply network).
77: pub const ISOLATED_STABILITY_PENALTY: u8 = 5;
78: 
79: /// Maximum per-turn stability penalty from a housing deficit.
80: ///
81: /// The actual penalty is `min(housing_deficit, MAX_HOUSING_DEFICIT_STABILITY_PENALTY)`.
82: pub const MAX_HOUSING_DEFICIT_STABILITY_PENALTY: u8 = 10;
83: 
84: /// Maximum per-turn stability penalty from unemployed population.
85: ///
86: /// The actual penalty is `min(unemployed, MAX_UNEMPLOYMENT_STABILITY_PENALTY)`.
87: pub const MAX_UNEMPLOYMENT_STABILITY_PENALTY: u8 = 5;
88: 
89: /// Maximum per-turn stability penalty from a food deficit while isolated.
90: ///
91: /// Only applied to colonies that are both food-deficient AND disconnected from
92: /// the empire supply network.
93: pub const MAX_ISOLATED_FOOD_DEFICIT_STABILITY_PENALTY: u8 = 5;
94: 
95: /// Stability lost per turn while a colony is under active blockade.
96: ///
97: /// **Changed from 5 → 8** to make blockades a meaningful strategic lever;
98: /// players and AI must now respond to blockades within roughly a dozen turns
99: /// before significant destabilisation occurs.
100: pub const BLOCKADED_STABILITY_PENALTY: u8 = 8;
101: 
102: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
103: // Internal stability & unrest
104: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
105: 
106: /// Number of turns a recently conquered colony carries explicit conquest unrest.
107: pub const CONQUEST_UNREST_TURNS: u32 = 12;
108: 
109: /// Colony count before overextension unrest pressure begins.
110: pub const OVEREXTENSION_COLONY_THRESHOLD: usize = 4;
111: 
112: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
113: // Combat and invasion
114: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
115: 
116: /// Base invasion strength contributed by a single Troop Transport ship.
117: ///
118: /// Total invasion strength = ships × (TROOP_TRANSPORT_INVASION_STRENGTH +
119: /// empire invasion bonus per transport).
120: pub const TROOP_TRANSPORT_INVASION_STRENGTH: u32 = 12;
121: 
122: /// Colony stability after a successful capture.
123: ///
124: /// **Changed from 40 → 45** so captured worlds are slightly less crippled
125: /// and can more quickly become productive for their new owner.
126: pub const CAPTURED_UNREST_STABILITY: u8 = 45;
127: 
128: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
129: // Diplomacy thresholds
130: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
131: 
132: /// Squared-distance threshold for routine border pressure.
133: ///
134: /// `40_000` ≈ 200 map units.  Close enough for neighbouring home systems and
135: /// early border colonies to feel contested without treating the whole sector
136: /// as immediate pressure.
137: pub const BORDER_TENSION_DISTANCE_SQ: i64 = 40_000;
138: 
139: /// Squared-distance threshold for severe border pressure.
140: ///
141: /// `12_000` ≈ 110 map units.  Very close frontier overlap; the AI is allowed
142: /// to escalate toward its harshest diplomacy posture.
143: pub const SEVERE_BORDER_TENSION_DISTANCE_SQ: i64 = 12_000;
144: 
145: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
146: // Fleet travel
147: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
148: 
149: /// Fleet travel speed in galaxy coordinate units per turn.
150: ///
151: /// Stars are generated in the range `-500..=500` on each axis, giving a
152: /// maximum possible distance of ≈1 414 units.  A speed of 500 yields:
153: ///
154: /// * dist ≤ 500 → 1 turn  (close-range, same or adjacent sectors)
155: /// * dist ≤ 1 000 → 2 turns (medium-range)
156: /// * dist > 1 000 → 3 turns (long-range, far sectors)
157: pub const FLEET_TRAVEL_SPEED: f64 = 500.0;
158: 
159: /// Hyperspace lane travel divisor.  Direct lanes halve travel duration
160: /// (rounded up), so a 3-turn flight becomes 2 turns.
161: pub const HYPERSPACE_TRAVEL_DIVISOR: u32 = 2;
162: 
163: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
164: // Maintenance scaling
165: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
166: 
167: /// Soft credit cap for total fleet maintenance per empire.
168: ///
169: /// Empires whose combined fleet maintenance exceeds this threshold receive
170: /// doubled upkeep on every fleet above the cap, discouraging fleet spam and
171: /// rewarding quality over quantity.
172: ///
173: /// Set to 50 credits/turn, which is roughly 8–10 mid-tier combat ships.
174: ///
175: /// **Reserved for future use** — this constant is not yet wired into the
176: /// engine's maintenance loop. It is defined here so the tuning decision is
177: /// recorded alongside other balance constants and can be referenced when the
178: /// fleet-spam mechanic is implemented.
179: pub const FLEET_MAINTENANCE_CREDIT_CAP_PER_EMPIRE: i64 = 50;

419:     requirements: DiscoveryRequirements,
420:     surveyed: bool,
421:     completed_techs: &[TechId],
422: ) -> bool {
423:     (!requirements.surveyed || surveyed)
424:         && requirements
425:             .required_techs
426:             .iter()
427:             .all(|tech| completed_techs.contains(tech))
428: }
